No advisory affecting 12.4.x has been published since 12.4.4. TWO METHODOLOGY TRAPS FOUND HERE, both of which would have produced a false finding, and both worth carrying forward because they will recur every cycle: (1) OSV IS UNUSABLE FOR THIS PACKAGE. Querying api.osv.dev for github.com/grafana/grafana at version 12.4.4 returns THIRTY-NINE vulns, which reads like an alarm; inspecting the records shows the 2026 ones carry ranges of literally [{introduced: '0'}] with NO fixed event, so they match EVERY version ever released. An OSV version query for grafana is a false-positive generator, not a scan. Use GHSA (which carries real ranges -- e.g. CVE-2025-41117 is >=12.2.0,<12.2.5 and >=12.3.0,<12.3.3, i.e. below the 12.4 line) or grafana.com/security/security-advisories. Note also that GHSA's Go-module ranges for CVE-2026-33380/33381 are pseudo-versions ('< 1.9.2-0.20260513165311-fb7336fc36c1') describing grafana-as-a-LIBRARY, which do not map to the OSS distribution's 12.x at all. (2) A WEB-SEARCH SUMMARIZER INVENTED A CVE. It asserted, twice and confidently, that 'CVE-2026-13438' was fixed in 12.4.7 and 13.0.5. That id DOES NOT EXIST: cveawg.mitre.org returns CVE_RECORD_DNE, it appears in no release body, and it is absent from Grafana's own advisory index. It was NOT filed. The rule this vindicates: search results are a pointer to a primary source, never a finding. PROBE (docker_escape_paths) -> REM-197, and the shape of it is the lesson: the grafana role's compose template does not stop at Grafana -- its tail renders the exporter fleet, and cAdvisor in that fleet is the single highest-privilege container in the estate. privileged:true, uid 0, SecurityOpt label=disable, host / at /rootfs, /sys + /var/lib/docker + /var/run bound, on observability_net AND the flat shared_net. The docker socket is LIVE and it took work to prove because the surface lies twice: `ls -l` shows /var/run/docker.sock as a symlink to /Users/pazny/.docker/run/docker.sock (the /var/run:ro bind shadows the explicit socket bind and drags in the macOS host's own /var/run), which reads as dangling -- but /proc/self/mountinfo shows /host-services/docker.proxy.sock bound at exactly that path, and cat returns ENXIO (it IS a socket) not ENOENT. And `:ro` on a socket bind is cosmetic: it blocks unlinking the file, not the API, which is request/response over that socket. docker info confirms no rootless and no Enhanced Container Isolation. So code execution in cAdvisor is host root via POST /containers/create {Privileged:true, Binds:['/:/host']}. WHAT MAKES IT ACTIONABLE RATHER THAN THEORETICAL IS THE VALUE SIDE, MEASURED: Prometheus holds ONE series for container_cpu_usage_seconds_total and ONE for container_memory_usage_bytes, both id='/' -- ZERO per-container metrics, which is cAdvisor's entire purpose. /api/v1.3/docker returns 0 containers. The log is an infinite 'failed to identify the read-write layer ID ... /rootfs/var/lib/docker/image/overlayfs/layerdb/...: no such file or directory' loop, because /rootfs is macOS while the real /var/lib/docker is inside the LinuxKit VM. Maximum privilege, no delivered value. Rated exploitable-post-foothold not remotely-triggerable: :8080 answers 200 unauthenticated to any shared_net peer (same host-map-is-not-a-network-gate error as REM-194) but serves only read-only metrics and no secret, and cAdvisor has no published CVE. Fix: drop it on Darwin, or route it through the docker-socket-proxy the estate ALREADY runs for portainer and traefik and de-privilege it. v0.49.1 vs upstream head v0.60.5 is hygiene only -- the privilege is in our compose file, not their release notes.

STATE AT CREATION: iiab-mcp-grafana-1 runs mcp/grafana pinned BY DIGEST to sha256:9362bcf6...4014 (roles/pazny.mcp_gateway/defaults/main.yml:76). The image's OCI label org.opencontainers.image.revision resolves to grafana/mcp-grafana commit 76ed7db (2026-07-07), which GitHub compare places 5 commits ahead of v0.17.0, exactly ONE commit behind v0.17.1, and 27 behind v1.1.0. SCHEDULING NOTE: `latest`-tagged and digest-pinned images defeat version-keyed scanning entirely -- the resident image can sit arbitrarily far behind upstream with nothing in the repo to show it. attack_probe_schedule.note: Cycle-16 batch-34 RE-SCAN over spacetimedb/nginx/vaultwarden/postgresql/ollama (2026-07-26, CVE scan + unauthenticated_endpoint_scan; 2-day re-check of the batch-33 cohort). 1 NEW item (REM-136, vaultwarden MEDIUM) + 1 closed (REM-135, spacetimedb). The probe's finding of record this batch: vaultwarden's unauth surface is WIDER than previously recorded. Prior batches leaned on the 127.0.0.1:8062 host bind to call the unauth legs 'LAN/insider-scoped', but that bind only constrains the DIRECT container port — traefik_auth_modes.vaultwarden='oidc' attaches NO forward-auth middleware to the auto-published Host(`pass.<tld>`) router, so anonymous HTTPS transits the edge into the app over iiab_net/shared_net. That makes the new icon-endpoint SSRF pair (GHSA-hw4g-2v3f-74x5, GHSA-vh5m-fc9v-m84g) and the unauth WebSocket flooding DDoS (GHSA-96f7-78q5-j345, against a hub that compose.yml.j2:23 enables unconditionally) anonymously reachable by anyone who can resolve the tenant TLD. Rated MEDIUM, not HIGH: SSRF is blind-ish and the WS leg is availability-only, SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=false, and no internet exposure unless the TLD is publicly routed. GENERAL LESSON for future native_oidc services: 'oidc' in traefik_auth_modes means the EDGE IS OPEN and the app's own login is the only gate — pre-auth endpoints (icons, websockets, health, well-known) of every native_oidc service are anonymously reachable and must be scored as such. The other four components re-confirmed with no anonymously-reachable exposure: spacetimedb (loopback host-map + install flag off), nginx (install_nginx=false default; Traefik is the edge), postgresql (loopback, no HTTP, no router), ollama (OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1 loopback bind is the sole control for the still-unpatched CVE-2026-5757).

attack_probe_schedule.name: version_header_leakage
attack_probe_schedule.description: Check HTTP response headers for version disclosure
attack_probe_schedule.note: Cycle-25 batch-48 SECOND RUN of this probe type, over mariadb/redis/infisical/rustfs/qgis_server (2026-08-10), completing the batch-47 attempt that died at write-back. 2 items filed (REM-189, REM-190, both MEDIUM, both rustfs). THE PROBE'S FINDING OF RECORD: fs.pazny.eu/health returns 200 anonymously with the exact string "version":"1.0.0-beta.11", and internet reach was PROVEN rather than assumed -- the request was re-issued against the public Cloudflare anycast address and came back with server: cloudflare, cf-ray ...-PRG and cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC, i.e. through the real edge to this origin, uncached. That is the evidentiary standard REM-144 explicitly could not meet (split-horizon dnsmasq had resolved its 'public' test back to the LAN, so it correctly refused to claim internet exposure); future probes should reach for --resolve against the authoritative public address before either claiming or disclaiming reach. It also overturns the 'pre-auth leg is CLOSED' disposition rustfs had carried since batch-36 -- the leg is not closed, it is narrowed to /health and /favicon.ico, and /health is the one that talks. THE GENERAL LESSON, which is about TIME rather than about headers: an advisory verdict is only true as of the hour it was read. REM-187 recorded rustfs's advisory leg clean at 04:12 and predicted, from this vendor's demonstrated habit of retroactively naming later releases as sole-patched, that beta.11 would likely acquire advisories anyway. Six were published at 14:13 the same day -- four against beta.11 and two against beta.12, the very version REM-187 recommended bumping TO. The prediction was right within ten hours, which means for a no-CVE prerelease vendor a clean verdict must carry its timestamp and a short shelf life. Pair that with the version disclosure above and the two findings compose: the estate publishes, anonymously and worldwide, exactly the string an attacker needs to know when this host's version enters an affected range. SECONDARY PATTERN, the probe's nominal quarry across all five: the components with NO HTTP surface are not automatically silent. MariaDB's pre-auth MySQL handshake advertises '11.8.8-MariaDB-ubu2404' -- application version AND Ubuntu base image -- to anyone who can open a socket, which is protocol-inherent and unfixable by config; Redis under --requirepass answers '-NOAUTH Authentication required.' to INFO, PING and LOLWUT alike and discloses nothing, a protocol-design difference rather than a configuration one. Neither is filed (both are loopback-bound with no router), but the sidecar observation is worth carrying: redis_exporter republishes redis_version="8.10.0" on an unauthenticated /metrics, so an exporter can undo the reticence its service carefully maintains. And qgis_server returns `Server: Apache/2.4.18 (Ubuntu)` -- one header fingerprinting a 2019 Ubuntu 16.04 userland -- which is not a new row but is the cleanest possible evidence for REM-184; it does not reach the internet only because REM-185's missing Authentik Provider makes the edge 404 first. --- PRIOR: Cycle-17 batch-38 FIRST RUN of this probe type, over woodpecker/jellyfin/traefik/uptime_kuma/calibreweb (2026-07-30): 4 items (REM-144 CRITICAL, REM-145 HIGH, REM-146 LOW, REM-147 LOW) + REM-148. Looking for leaked version strings surfaced leaked CREDENTIALS -- Traefik's dashboard/API answered anonymously at the edge because traefik_auth_modes.traefik='none', and /api/http/middlewares served rendered customRequestHeaders verbatim, disclosing X-Wing-Edge-Token, X-Face-Edge-Token and global_password_prefix itself. Lesson recorded there: 'oidc' means the edge is open and the app's own login is the only gate; 'none' means there is no gate at all. Also: security-headers@file strips NO response headers, it only adds, so any upstream Server or X-Powered-By passes through the edge untouched.

attack_probe_schedule.description: Check image age, CVE delta, and registry trust
attack_probe_schedule.note: Cycle-23 batch-44 FIRST RUN of this probe type, over mailpit/nginx/vaultwarden/ollama/spacetimedb (2026-08-06). 4 items filed: REM-171 (MEDIUM, mailpit CVE), REM-172 (MEDIUM, ollama provenance), REM-173 (LOW, spacetimedb freshness), REM-174 (LOW, gate coverage). THE PROBE'S FINDING OF RECORD: looking for stale PINS surfaced stale PROVENANCE, which is the more dangerous of the two because a version scan cannot see it. Two of the four findings are cases where the version number was never wrong and the estate still could not prove it. (1) ollama: the pinned-free `state: latest` install has been the stated basis for closing REM-096 since April -- but the binary actually running is pazny/local/ollama 0.30.7_1 from an operator-authored tap the playbook has never heard of, so the freshness claim is unmeasured, and a fresh blank would install a DIFFERENT core-tap binary that cannot serve GGUF at all. The claim and the estate agreed by luck. (2) The image-pin gate: test_image_pin_hygiene.py reads variable DECLARATIONS but not the RENDER SITE, and 28 role compose templates fall back to `| default('latest')` (mailpit to an ancient v1.20). Measured honestly, 0 of the 28 are reachable today -- every var still has a declaration -- which is why it is filed LOW. But 1bc5dcbb's shadow deletion left exactly ONE declaration per pin, so a single deleted line is now the whole distance between a pinned tag and `latest`, through a gate that stays green because a deleted variable declares nothing to scan. That is the gate's own docstring warning ('scanning only one of two files is how a gate loses scope silently') one surface further out. GENERAL LESSON, the mirror of cycle-19/20's 'a GHSA with no CVE id': scanning versions answers 'is the number old', never 'is the number load-bearing'. A supply-chain scan must ask where the artifact CAME FROM and what would happen if the pin were deleted -- neither question is answerable from a version string. Counter-example kept deliberately: nginx runs the SAME unpinned `state: latest` pattern as ollama and is correctly rated CLEAN, because it is off by default and its upstream ships fixes promptly. Same mechanism, opposite verdict; the pattern is not the finding, the surrounding facts are.
